Proposal

Known URLs answered from the recipe

proposal/known-urls-from-the-recipe2026-11-02Giovanni Porcaridraft

Problem

External clients read some documents at fixed paths of a site. Examples: /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116), /robots.txt, /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS universal links), /.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android app links).

The content of these documents depends on the deployment, not on the code: a contact address, the crawler rules, the identifiers of a mobile app. The same application code runs on sites that need different values.

In kajenn an application serves a /.well-known/ document only by declaring it in its code. A fixed path outside /.well-known/, such as /robots.txt, has no mechanism of its own. A site cannot declare these documents in its recipe.

genropy legacy answers these four documents from the instance configuration, with no code per site.

Current state

The proposal channels-meta-and-server-gui moves the branch _well_known to _meta/well_known. The public path /.well-known/ does not change. This proposal holds for both locations.

Proposed solution

Behaviour

  • The recipe declares, at site level, the documents the site answers at fixed paths. Each declaration carries the data of the document, not its text.
  • kajenn generates the body from that data, with the media type the standard requires. No application code is needed.
  • The first set is the legacy one: security.txt, robots.txt, apple-app-site-association, assetlinks.json.
  • A document not declared in the recipe does not exist: its path follows today's rules (404 under /.well-known/, normal demux elsewhere). There is no runtime exception for a missing configuration.
  • Wrong data is refused at boot, not at request time.
  • Applications keep declaring their own /.well-known/ documents in code, as today.

Where the recipe documents are answered

ServerApplication is always mounted. It can carry the recipe documents as children of its own _well_known branch. /.well-known/<name> then reaches it through the index that exists today, with no change to demux_hidden. Decision d-owner compares this with the alternatives.

A root path such as /robots.txt has no existing mechanism. Decision d-root covers it.

Example recipe shape

Element and attribute names are placeholders until the decisions below are taken.

Decisions

opend-scope
Which documents are in the first cut?
  1. The four legacy documents

    Pro: parity with genropy legacy; every format is already known. Con: none known.

  2. The legacy four plus openid-configuration, change-password and sitemap.xml

    Pro: covers more probes. Con: code for documents no site asks for today.

opend-owner
Which component answers the recipe documents?
  1. ServerApplication, in its _well_known branch

    Pro: ServerApplication is always mounted; the existing index routes /.well-known/ with no demux change. Con: _server gains a role that is not administration.

  2. The server demux, before the application index

    Pro: works with no application at all. Con: the demux generates content, which today it never does.

  3. An application the site declares in the recipe

    Pro: explicit; uses only today's mechanism. Con: every site that wants one document must add an application.

opend-root
How is a root path outside /.well-known/ (/robots.txt) answered?
  1. An exact-path index in the demux, checked before the mount lookup

    Pro: same rule as legacy; one dict lookup. Con: a site path shadows a mount with the same first segment.

  2. Left to the root application, as today

    Pro: no change. Con: a site with no root application cannot answer /robots.txt.

  3. Only /.well-known/ documents are in scope

    Pro: smallest change. Con: robots.txt, part of the legacy set, is left out.

opend-conflict
What happens when an application declares a name the recipe also declares?
  1. Boot fails with FatalBootError

    Pro: no silent winner. Con: an external application that joins later cannot be refused at boot.

  2. The recipe wins

    Pro: the site has the last word over application code. Con: changes today's rule (the last registered wins).

  3. Today's rule: the last registered wins

    Pro: no new rule. Con: the result depends on registration order.

opend-static
Does SiteHome.static also serve files at fixed paths (favicon.ico, sitemap.xml)?
  1. No, out of this proposal

    Pro: keeps generated documents and static files apart. Con: SiteHome.static stays a folder nobody serves.

  2. Yes, through the same exact-path index

    Pro: one place for every fixed path. Con: depends on d-root.

Consequences

  • The recipe grammar gains a site-level element and one child per document type.
  • No new dependency: every format is plain text or JSON.
  • A genropy site moved to kajenn writes the same data in the recipe instead of wku.* and mobile_app.*.
  • With d-root-exact, the demux gains one lookup before the mount lookup.
